brief: JPMorgan reiterates Overweight on Meta, PT $820 (Dec-27, ~23x 2028E GAAP EPS of $35.44), after its 9/10/26 upgrade. Meta shares are up 21% since Muse launched two weeks ago versus the SPX's 1% gain. Muse is now the #1 downloaded free app in the US, with daily downloads exceeding every other Meta Family of Apps product. JPM ties this to product-market fit, a generous free tier (100M free weekly tokens versus paid Grok Bot and Gemini Spark), and Meta's distribution. JPM frames the opportunity in two steps: near term Meta prioritizes adoption and engagement, with monetization beyond heavy-user subscriptions unlikely before 2027. Opening Muse Connectors to outside developers is the first step toward businesses building agents on Muse, shifting transactions toward agent-to-agent interactions and unlocking a take-rate or commission model like advertising. Amazon has already blocked Muse access, though JPM still expects broader ecosystem participation over time. JPM flags investor caution ahead of Meta Connect, on views Muse had launched, Watermelon would come after Connect, and OpenAI would ship a rival agent this week, as a likely driver of Monday's outsized move in Meta shares. JPM expects Connect to cover AI and agent progress, not a Watermelon launch.
